Drop Site Daily: October 9, 2026 | | | Oct 9 | | | | | | | | | | | | | | ---|---|--- South African lawyer Navanethem "Navi" Pillay speaks at the Nuremberg Forum in Nuremberg following the announcement that she will be awarded the 2026 Nobel Peace Prize. Photo by Daniel Karmann/picture alliance via Getty Images. Friday, October 9, 2026 -** Palestine : Israeli attacks kill nine Palestinians in Gaza on Thursday and Friday. Israeli settlers carry out at least 19 attacks across the occupied West Bank, targeting olive harvesters and property. Palestinian Authority plans to postpone November elections until September 2027. Nearly 22,000 Palestinian children killed in Israeli attacks on Gaza over three years, with more than 71,000 orphaned. Israeli military actions linked to deaths of at least 24 captives in Gaza, CNN investigation finds. Colombia to open Israel embassy in Jerusalem next week. Yemen : Three killed in Ansarallah attacks on Saudi airport. Saudi-led coalition destroys three Ansarallah missile launchers as airstrikes reported in Sana'a. Iran : President Donald Trump says U.S. will not attack Iran before the November 3 midterms. Russian President Vladimir Putin tells Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian Russia will "do everything" to help end the U.S.-led war. Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps strikes LPG tanker, threatens to target vessels beyond Strait of Hormuz. At least 81 U.S. military aircraft lost or damaged in war against Iran, costing up to $3.3 billion. U.S. sanctions 17 more vessels carrying Iranian oil. Lebanon: Israeli forces uproot olive trees in southern Lebanon amid airstrikes and artillery shelling. U.S. : ICE agent shoots and wounds man in New York City with 5-year-old in car. Trump disclosed 517 securities trades in August, including up to $25 million in Meta and SpaceX debt bought two days before a space policy signing. Pentagon to livestream firing-squad execution of Fort Hood shooter. FBI deletes video attacking Democrats. Trump administration suspends Microsoft, seven other firms from green card program, alleging fraud. Michigan Republican Senate nominee Mike Rogers leaves door open to AIPAC support in Michigan Senate race. International: Navi Pillay, who led UN inquiry finding Israel committed genocide in Gaza, wins Nobel Peace Prize. Ukrainian strikes kill two in Russia's Belgorod; Russian bombs kill one in Zaporizhzhia. No survivors from sunken ship off Bulgaria. Ethiopia tells UN Security Council it will defend itself against Eritrean "all-out invasion." Drone strikes hit Eritrean forces inside northern Ethiopia, conflict monitor says. Brazilian justice issues arrest warrant for Eduardo Bolsonaro weeks before runoff. France pledges 3,000 extra teachers as student protests continue; stun grenades banned from marches. Prison fight in Sinaloa kills 10, including a minor. U.S. judge orders Trump administration to facilitate return of Egyptian man deported to Equatorial Guinea. UN Security Council extends Sudan sanctions by two months. South Africa withdraws asylum intake directive after anti-migrant protests turn violent. International Criminal Court judges rule former Philippine President Rodrigo Duterte fit to stand trial; trial opens November 30. This is Drop Site Daily, our free news recap We send it Monday - Friday Palestine Israeli attacks kill nine Palestinians in Gaza on Thursday and Friday: Israeli forces killed at least nine Palestinians and wounded several others across the Gaza Strip on Thursday and Friday, according to WAFA. On Friday, Israeli troops on Palestinians east of the Maghazi and Bureij refugee camps in central Gaza, killing one man who was shot in the neck and wounding others. On Thursday, eight Palestinians were killed in Israeli attacks, including two men in a drone strike on a vehicle near the Jordanian field hospital in southwest Gaza City, a woman in artillery shelling northwest of the city, and two people, including a child, in a drone strike on a home in the Sabra neighborhood. Israeli settlers carry out at least 19 attacks across the occupied West Bank, targeting olive harvesters and property: Israeli settlers at least 19 attacks across the occupied West Bank on Friday, assaulting olive harvesters, burning vehicles and trees, stealing livestock, and forcing farmers off their land, according to the Palestinian Wall and Settlement Resistance Commission. Israeli forces also fired live ammunition and tear gas at farmers, confiscated agricultural equipment, and conducted raids and arrests. Nablus: Settlers olive harvesters across several villages, including Tal, Jamma'in, Qusra, Beita, Sebastia, Beit Furik, and Deir Sharaf, forcing farmers off their land. They burned a vehicle in Tal and uprooted more than 50 olive trees in Qusra, where Israeli soldiers fired tear gas and stun grenades, sparking fires. Ramallah: Settlers farmers in Deir Sudan and Deir Ibzi, stealing crops and forcing them off their land. Armed settlers stole 20 sheep in Ein Qiniya under Israeli military protection, while a man and his child were assaulted and their vehicle stolen in Yabroud. Two people were injured in settler attacks in Deir Ibzi. Salfit: Israeli soldiers and settlers live ammunition to drive farmers from their land in Deir Ballut, while settlers injured a farmer in Kafr ad-Dik. Settlers also burned olive trees in Wadi Al-Shaer. Hebron: A 79-year-old woman was after settlers unleashed dogs on olive harvesters in Birin. Israeli forces confiscated a school transport vehicle, two tractors and animal feed in Masafer Yatta, and arrested nine Palestinians in Hebron, including the director of the Ibrahimi Mosque. Jenin: Settlers 100 olive trees in Al-Mughayyir village overnight Thursday. Palestinian Authority plans to postpone November elections until September 2027: Palestinian Authority Vice President Hussein Al-Sheikh France that legislative elections scheduled for November 28 will be postponed, potentially until September 2027, citing worsening political, security and economic conditions in Gaza and the occupied West Bank, according to an October 8 letter seen by Reuters. The letter pointed to a number of causes for the postponement, including expectations of an Israeli withdrawal from Gaza, the deployment of international forces and Palestinian police, curbs on Israeli annexation and settler violence, and the release of nearly $7 billion in Palestinian funds withheld by Israel, that had not materialized. Palestinians have not held legislative elections since 2006 or presidential elections since 2005, and Palestinian Authority President Mahmoud Abbas has ruled by decree since his presidential mandate expired in 2009. Hamas won a majority over Fatah in the January 2006 Palestinian parliamentary elections, prompting severe Israeli economic and military measures against the Hamas-led government. Nearly 22,000 Palestinian children killed in Israeli attacks on Gaza over three years, with more than 71,000 orphaned: Israeli attacks killed at least 21,976 Palestinian children in Gaza over the past three years, an average of one child every 71 minutes, according to a report by Gaza's Health Ministry. Among those killed were 5,444 children under five and 1,125 infants under one year old. Another 45,569 children have been injured, including 1,134 who have undergone amputations, while 71,846 have been orphaned. The ministry also reported 612 children killed while seeking food or medicine, 466 deaths from malnutrition, including 157 children, and 2,027 patients who died while awaiting medical evacuation, including 264 children. The report found that all 38 hospitals and 158 primary healthcare centers in Gaza have been targeted, with 19 hospitals and 64 healthcare centers out of service. It also documented 1,723 healthcare workers killed and 216 ambulances targeted. Israeli military actions linked to deaths of at least 24 captives in Gaza, CNN investigation finds: At least 24 of the 40 Israeli captives who died in captivity in Gaza had , including airstrikes and ground operations, as well as military advances that prompted their captors to kill them, a CNN investigation found. At least 11 were killed directly by Israeli military operations. The investigation, based on interviews with captive families and Israeli officials, also found that Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu repeatedly delayed ceasefire negotiations, including a potential deal in July 2024 that officials said could have saved lives. Colombia to open Israel embassy in Jerusalem next week: Israeli Foreign Minister Gideon Saar Thursday that Colombia will inaugurate its embassy to Israel in Jerusalem "next Wednesday," as he touted expanding ties with Latin America. A Colombian Foreign Ministry official told AFP that Foreign Minister Omar Bula Escobar will travel to Jerusalem on Sunday ahead of the opening. Abelardo De la Espriella, Colombia's new right-wing president, promised close relations with Israel during his campaign. Once elected, he restored diplomatic ties with Israel that left-wing President Gustavo Petro had severed as a result of Israel's genocide in Gaza. Israel occupied East Jerusalem in 1967 and annexed it in 1980 in a move largely unrecognized internationally, claiming the entire city as its capital, while Palestinians seek Jerusalem as the capital of a future Palestinian state. Yemen Three killed in Ansarallah attacks on Saudi airport: Three Saudi citizens were killed and several others injured in two Ansarallah on King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh on Thursday, according to Saudi Arabia's Civil Aviation Authority. One attack targeted airport facilities, while the other struck a Saudi Airlines aircraft on the ground, killing an airline employee and damaging the plane, which had no passengers aboard. Hundreds of flights to Riyadh were cancelled, though flight cancellations fell from 335 on Thursday to at least 103 on Friday as the airport worked to restore normal operations. The EU Aviation Safety Agency also expanded its warning against flying over parts of Saudi Arabia, citing Ansarallah' demonstrated ability to strike targets deeper inside the kingdom, including Riyadh. Saudi-led coalition destroys three Ansarallah missile launchers as airstrikes reported in Sana 'a: The Saudi-led coalition said it destroyed three missile launch platforms used by Ansarallah, releasing of the strikes. Separately, Ansarallah-affiliated Al-Masira airstrikes on Yemen's capital, Sana'a, without immediately providing details on casualties or damage. Iran Trump says U.S. will not attack Iran before the Nov. 3 midterms : President Donald Trump on Truth Social Thursday that "we will not be attacking Iran at any time prior to the Midterm Elections to be held in the United States on November 3rd." He justified this further in the post by claiming that Iran is "in very bad condition, both Economically and Militarily." He has repeatedly tied the war to the midterms, saying he believes Iran's leaders are trying to hold out through November to hurt Republicans, and that he expects to win the war after the vote. Putin tells Iran 's Pezeshkian Russia will "do everything" to help end the U.S.-led war: Russian President Vladimir** Putin Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian in Turkmenistan on Thursday, ahead of the Commonwealth of Independent States summit, and said, "On our part, we are ready to do everything we can to help you resolve this situation," according to the Interfax news service. The Russian president commended Iran for making "real efforts to end the conflict, which broke out through no fault of its own," and noted a "positive evolution" in Iran-Russia ties. On Wednesday, Putin told Pezeshkian in a call that Moscow is ready to mediate between the U.S. and Iran, Iran's IRNA reported. Pezeshkian said talks with the U.S. to end the war could succeed only if based on "mutual respect and reciprocal commitments" and free from "pressure and threats," speaking at the summit on Friday. Iran 's IRGC strikes LPG tanker, threatens to target vessels beyond Strait of Hormuz: Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) it struck a large LPG tanker named NV Sunshine attempting to transit an "illegal route" south of the Strait of Hormuz, causing a major fire in its engine room and propulsion system, according to Tasnim news agency. The IRGC subsequently warned that vessels using unauthorized routes would face "punitive measures" even outside the strait, threatening to pursue them "throughout the region" and warning against following "deception of the American aggressors." At least 81 U.S. military aircraft lost or damaged in war against Iran, costing up to $3.3 billion: At least 81 U.S. military aircraft were lost or damaged during Operation Epic Fury, Washington's military campaign against Iran launched on February 28, according to a Congressional Budget Office report. The report estimated losses of $1.9 billion to $3.3 billion as of August 1, including 12 F-15E fighter jets, one F-35A, seven KC-135 refueling aircraft and 45 MQ-9 Reaper drones. U.S. sanctions 17 more vessels carrying Iranian oil: The U.S. Treasury Department sanctions on 17 additional vessels linked to Iran's so-called "shadow fleet" as part of its "Operation Economic Outcast" campaign to cut Tehran's oil revenues amid the ongoing war. The vessels, registered across more than a dozen jurisdictions, have transported millions of barrels of Iranian crude and petroleum products, according to the Treasury. A U.S. official said Iran has stopped loading and unloading oil because of the American blockade of its ports, while shipping data firm Kpler reported no Iranian crude loaded for export since August 25. Lebanon Israeli forces uproot olive trees in southern Lebanon amid airstrikes and artillery shelling: Nabatieh: Israeli infantry accompanied by a D9 bulldozer advanced to within 50 meters of a Lebanese army position in Zawtar Al-Gharbiyeh, continuing to in an operation that began Thursday, according to Lebanon's National News Agency. Israeli warplanes also struck the outskirts of Kfar Tebnit, following overnight shelling near Nabatieh Al-Fawqa, Kfar Tebnit and Mayfadoun. Marjayoun: An Israeli Merkava tank advanced from Khiam toward the Ibl al-Saqi spring, with Israeli forces firing machine guns toward the surrounding area. Artillery also struck Wadi Al-Salouqi. Tyre (Sour): Israeli forces shelled Mansouri, Majdal Zoun and surrounding valleys overnight. Bint Jbeil: Israeli shelling Wadi Zibqin and areas near Baraachit and Hadatha. U.S. News ICE agent shoots and wounds man in New York City with 5-year-old in car: An ICE agent seven rounds into a car around 4 p.m. Thursday in New York City's Marble Hill neighborhood, wounding Oscar Belgal , 28, in the neck below the left ear, according to New York City Police Commissioner Jessica Tisch. A 5-year-old boy believed to be his son was in the back seat and was not injured. Surveillance video of the incident showed a plainclothes officer approaching the driver's window with his gun drawn before the car began to move, Tisch noted. DHS said agents were trying to arrest an undocumented Dominican immigrant with a grand larceny conviction, but did not name Belgal, explain why the agent fired, or whether the agent knew a child was in the car. The New York City Police Department said its officers were not involved. New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani called the shooting "an outrage," saying "there is no justification for what we have seen today." Mamdani also claimed that during a two hour call with President Donald Trump and Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin they refused to release Belgal, whom ICE took away in an unmarked vehicle. New York Governor Kathy Hochul said she urged Trump and Mullin to halt ICE operations in New York and asked that any body-camera footage be released. Protesters gathered at the scene and outside Allen Hospital, where officers scuffled with them and at least one person was detained. Incoming Rep. Darializa Avila Chevalier . Immigration agents have shot at least two dozen people across the country since January 2025, killing six, including three U.S. citizens. Trump disclosed 517 securities trades in August, including up to $25 million in Meta and SpaceX debt bought two days before a space policy signing: Trump's August financial disclosure 517 purchases and sales totaling roughly $74.3 million to $273.3 million, according to a CNBC analysis, with purchases of at least $44.2 million and sales of at least $30.1 million. The largest was an August 21 purchase of $5 million to $25 million in Meta stock. On August 18, Trump's accounts bought $1 million to $5 million in senior unsecured SpaceX notes at 5.35 percent, maturing in 2031. Two days later, he signed a national space transportation policy calling for more than 1,000 launches and reentries a year by 2030. SpaceX is a major Pentagon contractor and NASA launch provider. On August 26, his portfolio bought $15,001 to $50,000 of Tyson Foods the same day he signed a proclamation expanding low-tariff imports of lean beef trimmings. The disclosure does not show whether the trade came before or after the signing. Trump's 2025 annual disclosure showed more than 21,000 trades across eight accounts holding at least $858 million, which contrasts starkly with the 86 stock transactions he made during the first year of his first term, in 2017. Pentagon to livestream firing-squad execution of Fort Hood shooter: War Secretary Pete Hegseth Real America's Voice on Thursday that Nidal Hasan , convicted of killing 13 people in the 2009 Fort Hood shooting, "is gonna get a firing squad of soldiers. As it should be." He added, "We'll make sure that people are able to watch it. That it's public. Because people need to understand that there's serious consequences for these types of things." Hasan is scheduled to be executed December 3 at Fort Hood. The Pentagon later released a statement confirming that the execution will be livestreamed. The U.S. hasn't held a public execution since 1936, when Rainey Bethea was hanged in Kentucky. It would be the first US military execution since 1961. The last military firing-squad execution was in 1945. FBI deletes video attacking Democrats : An FBI video Tuesday on its rapid response X account labeled prominent Democrats, among them Kamala Harris , Reps. Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez and Ilhan Omar , former Rep.Cori Bush and Michigan Senate nominee Abdul El-Sayed , as part of "the DEFUND THE POLICE crowd," and accused them of seeking to "let criminals run wild while cops take a backseat." The FBI has since deleted the post and did not respond to a request for comment. Citizens for Responsibility and Ethics in Washington (CREW) filed a complaint with the Office of Special Counsel, which investigates violations of the Hatch Act, which limits the partisan political activities of federal executive branch employees (excluding the President). CREW CEO Donald Sherman said in an X post on Thursday that although the video does not tell viewers how to vote, its message that the candidates' policies "failed" is "advocacy against their election." He added that tagging El-Sayed as "Progressive Democrat, Senate Nominee" "clearly invokes the election." Trump administration suspends Microsoft, seven other firms from green card program, alleging fraud : Vice President JD Vance Thursday that the administration is suspending Microsoft, Adobe and tech consulting firms Cognizant, Infosys, Tata, Wipro, HCL and Capgemini from the H-1B visa program that allows foreign workers to apply for green cards. Vance accused the firms of hiding the job offers they are required to first publicly announce in the U.S. in "small town newspapers." He also claimed that Microsoft laid off 6,000 American workers last year while obtaining 6,300 H-1B visas and almost 3,000 green cards. Microsoft said about 80 percent of its roughly 6,000 H-1B filings last fiscal year were to extend or change the status of existing employees, and that the rest were for people already legally in the U.S. Vance also singled out nine universities for investigation over J-1 visa use: Harvard, Yale, Stanford, Brown, Pittsburgh, UC Davis, Caltech, Arizona State and MIT. MIT, Brown and Pitt said they had received subpoenas related to this investigation. The announcement came hours before Trump awarded the National Medal of Technology and Innovation to Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella. Rogers leaves door open to AIPAC support in Michigan Senate race : Michigan GOP Senate nominee Mike Rogers at a Thursday debate that he would accept AIPAC's backing against Democrat Abdul El-Sayed , saying "anybody that wants to help my campaign stop" El-Sayed, "I'll take all of that help." AIPAC's super PAC, United Democracy Project, spent more than $30 million against El-Sayed in the Michigan Democratic primary. AdImpact data show the group does not appear to have bought TV ads since. An August Axios report said Rogers' allies had asked AIPAC not to advertise for him, and that the group scrapped an anti-El-Sayed video a day after Rogers spoke with AIPAC board Chair Michael Tuchin. Rogers believed, according to Axios, that the group might be a liability to him in the general election, though around the time of his initial rupture with the group, he reportedly attended AIPAC-hosted fundraisers in California in August. 📥 Have a tip on Capitol Hill? Email DC Correspondent Julian Andreone at Julian@dropsitenews.com Other International News Ukrainian strikes kill two in Russia 's Belgorod; Russian bombs kill one in Zaporizhzhia: A Ukrainian strike two people and injured four, including a child, in the Russian border region of Belgorod on Friday, the Russian news agency TASS reported. A separate drone attack on the central region of Kaluga injured nine. In Ukraine, Russian bombs reportedly killed one person and injured seven, including a child, in Zaporizhzhia, according to the region's governor. No survivors from sunken ship off Bulgaria: Bulgarian authorities said they had found no survivors from the recently sunken Alfa Watan ship, one of two commercial vessels sunk by a drone in the Black Sea on Tuesday. Both of the sunken ships were managed by Turkey-based companies, according to Equasis. A Syrian customs official AFP on Thursday nine of the ten missing crew members on the recently sunken Alfa Watan were Syrians and the tenth was Egyptian. Navi Pillay, who led UN inquiry finding Israel committed genocide in Gaza, wins Nobel Peace Prize: South African jurist Navi Pillay, 85, was awarded the 2026 Nobel Peace Prize on Friday as "as a driving force in the development of an international system of law and order." A former UN human rights chief, ICC judge and anti-apartheid advocate, Pillay chaired the UN inquiry that concluded last year that Israel committed genocide in Gaza. Pillay learned of the award at a legal conference in Nuremberg, Germany, where Nazi leaders were tried after World War II. "The last thing I did is the delivery of the report on Gaza, naming what's happening there as genocide," she . In response to the award, Israel's Foreign Ministry Pillay of spreading "lies, hatred, and blood libels" and promoting what it called the "genoLIE." "Now that the Nobel commission has rewarded the biggest lie of the 21st century, Joseph Goebbels is certainly applauding from hell," it added, invoking the Nazi propaganda minister. Ethiopia tells UN Security Council it will defend itself against Eritrean "all-out invasion": Ethiopia in a letter to the UN Security Council that it has no option but to defend itself against what it described as an "all out invasion" by Eritrea, in its first official statement on reported Eritrean incursions earlier this week, according to Reuters. Foreign Minister Gedion Timothewos wrote that Eritrean forces, "including mechanized units," have deployed up to 60 km (37 miles) into northern Ethiopia. He called the Eritrean incursions a "matter of public record" and "a blatant act of aggression that engages Ethiopia's inherent right to self-defense." Witnesses told Reuters this week they saw Eritrean soldiers in northern Ethiopia, days after the two countries severed diplomatic ties. Ethiopia accuses Eritrea of backing a rebel alliance fighting federal troops since September 23 in Tigray, Amhara and Afar. Drone strikes hit Eritrean forces inside northern Ethiopia, conflict monitor says : Drone strikes, believed to have been carried out by Ethiopia's military, Eritrean military vehicles near Adigrat as they withdrew from positions in Tigray on Wednesday and Thursday, according to the U.S.-based conflict monitor ACLED. Eritrean soldiers crossed into Ethiopia on Wednesday, advanced dozens of kilometers, then pulled back under heavy bombardment, the conflict monitor added. Two sources, a diplomat and a conflict expert in contact with both sides, reported that Eritrean forces were moving north but said it was unclear whether they were leaving Ethiopia or redeploying within it. Brazilian justice issues arrest warrant for Eduardo Bolsonaro weeks before runoff : Supreme Court Justice Alexandre de Moraes an arrest warrant Thursday for Eduardo Bolsonaro, brother of presidential candidate Flavio Bolsonaro, ordering him to begin serving a four-year sentence immediately. Moraes cancelled Bolsonaro's passport and told federal police to arrest him should he return from Texas, where he currently resides, The Supreme Court convicted Eduardo in June of lobbying the U.S. to interfere in the trial of his father, former President Jair Bolsonaro, alleging that he lobbied for the U.S. to impose sanctions on Brazilian officials and tariffs on Brazilian exports. Jair Bolsonaro was sentenced in September 2025 to 27 years for plotting a coup, in an investigation chaired by de Moraes, whom the Bolsonaro family regards as a political enemy. The presidential election runoff between President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva and Flavio Bolsonaro is set for October 25. France pledges 3,000 extra teachers as student protests continue; stun grenades banned from marches: French Education Minister Edouard Geffray on Thursday that 3,000 teachers would be sent to high-priority schools by Tuesday, with a "few hundred more" to be recruited, after weeks of mass protests that have gripped the country. Nearly 71,500 people protested across France on Thursday, with 24,500 protesters reported in Paris alone, France's Interior Ministry said. More than 500 people were arrested. Economy Minister Roland Lescure added, following the 1.4% increase in money allocated for education in France's 2027 budget, that there was "room" to meet the demands of the protesters for more resources. The protests began September 21 at a school in a deprived Paris area. Initiated by high school students, the demonstrations have grown to include university students and trade unions. Demands have included more teachers, renovated buildings and fewer classroom hours. Police have been accused of using excessive force, with the use of stun grenades being banned after a teenager lost his hand to a police stun grenade earlier this week. Prison fight in Sinaloa kills 10, including a minor: A fight inside the El Castillo Penitentiary Centre in Mazatlan, Sinaloa, nine prisoners and a family visitor dead and 16 prisoners injured, state authorities said Thursday. A state official also added that the family visitor killed in the fight was a minor. Mexican security forces reportedly moved into the prison, and officials report that the prison is now "under control." Sinaloa is a battleground for warring factions of the Sinaloa drug cartel, and the State Department advises Americans not to visit it. Officials have not said whether the violence was linked to that conflict. U.S. judge orders Trump administration to facilitate return of Egyptian man deported to Equatorial Guinea : U.S. District Judge John C. Hinderaker Thursday that the Department of Homeland Security must facilitate the release of Ahmed Soliman from custody in Equatorial Guinea and his return to the U.S., Reuters reported. Soliman was deported to the central African country this year under a third-country deportation deal. Last month he said Equatorial Guinean police treated him roughly, and video obtained by Reuters showed officers pulling firearms on migrants, including him. After Reuters published this story, he was taken into custody and has been held incommunicado at a gendarmerie station. Soliman told an immigration judge last year he feared being killed in Egypt because he is gay. Reuters has documented 40 cases of migrants granted U.S. protection over persecution for their LGBT status who were deported to African countries that criminalize same-sex relations or have been described by the State Department as hostile to LGBT people. UN Security Council extends Sudan sanctions by two months: The Security Council unanimously on Thursday to extend sanctions on arms sales to warring factions in Darfur until December 11, 2026, after the United States withdrew a draft that would have broadened the scope of the sanctions to cover the whole of Sudan and all of its warring parties. Several member states reportedly wanted a standard one-year renewal of the Darfur embargo, which date back to 2005, without changes. Russia, which holds a veto, notably opposed the U.S. proposal to widen the sanctions regime. South Africa withdraws asylum intake directive after anti-migrant protests turn violent: South Africa's Home Affairs Department Friday it had withdrawn a directive allowing it to resume processing asylum applications, a day after anti-migrant protests turned violent in Johannesburg and Durban. The directive would have implemented a July 7 Constitutional Court ruling that found that asylum seekers could not be denied access to the system solely on "procedural grounds," meaning primarily that those who had entered the country illegally would not be automatically disqualified from asylum. The department said the proposed directive was withdrawn after the number of asylum applications overwhelmed refugee reception offices within days of its announcement, putting officials at risk and threatening public safety and order On Thursday, rioters torched 14 vehicles in Durban and 10 in Johannesburg's Soweto township, and foreign-owned shops were looted. A months-long surge in anti-immigrant protests in South Africa has strained its relations with other African countries and forced thousands of foreign nationals to leave. ICC judges rule Duterte fit to stand trial; trial opens Nov. 30: International Criminal Court judges in a September 28 decision, announced Thursday, that former Philippine President Rodrigo Duterte, 81, is fit to stand trial on crimes against humanity charges tied to his drug war. An independent expert panel found he "has the capacity to understand the charges," follow proceedings, understand the evidence, and discuss his defense with lawyers. body:
Plus: a $3.7B deal that'll support around 14K jobs
---
| | | | |
---
| My fellow Marylanders, We're moving Maryland forward on the issues that matter most to our people, including **building more housing, fighting for Maryland families, and strengthening our state’s economy.** Here’s how we've been taking on the housing crisis: I’ve signed two executive orders to [cut red tape, speed up permits, and make it easier to build homes](https://links-1.govdelivery.com/CL0/https:%2F%2Fwww.youtube.com%2Fwatch%3Fv=UxQzQYfjVxg/1/010001a12141a71c-0c895b63-ba06-4126-bf77-106c82cff7ee-000000/MbJaiUcvY35kLnFMNqsRAM48ER3IcFsdcmHZJuvS6zI=452), and we announced $17.6 million to create or preserve hundreds of affordable rental homes in seven counties and Baltimore City. We also announced a record $32 million through our ENOUGH Initiative to **fight child poverty** in communities across the state. In Frederick alone, this work has brought free vision screenings to over 1,000 students and set up almost 100 mobile produce markets for local families. In the face of the Trump-Vance Administration’s continued threats to benefits that families depend on, we’ve helped nearly [40,000 Marylanders maintain their access to SNAP](https://links-1.govdelivery.com/CL0/https:%2F%2Fgovernor.maryland.gov%2Fnews%2Fpress-releases%2Fgovernor-moore-reinforces-commitment-keep-marylanders%23:~:text=DHS%2520estimates%2520that,their%2520nutrition%2520benefits./1/010001a12141a71c-0c895b63-ba06-4126-bf77-106c82cff7ee-000000/weriKMHwoHpBX1fzhEaJZTLgltmuLxWvorHBafjqAy0=452). Maryland now ranks among the top 10 states for helping families on SNAP keep their nutrition benefits. And for the third year in a row, our **SUN Bucks program has helped feed more than 600,000 students this summer.** And [we just closed a deal with Anduril Industries](https://links-1.govdelivery.com/CL0/https:%2F%2Fwww.youtube.com%2Fwatch%3Fv=f-nsWaH-cKE/1/010001a12141a71c-0c895b63-ba06-4126-bf77-106c82cff7ee-000000/z9JFHn7kw9MoCOwBKwtsIrEghAuEaxQHixzJyM8-kjU=452) to expand Maryland’s manufacturing industry. This deal will drive **$3.7 BILLION in private investment** and **support around 14,000 jobs** , making it the largest private investment our state’s seen in over a decade. This major win builds on the multiple new business expansions we’ve seen over just the last few weeks. Thank you for your continued support and all you do to make this state a stronger, safer, and better place for those around you. Your Governor,
Wes Moore

body:
Ectopic pregnancy deaths nearly doubled. The steepest rise is in states with bans. | | | [](https://click.everyaction.com/k/141036524/652322197/2141984067?sourceid=1151673&utm_campaign=27emcus-1001aax-on&utm_medium=ea&utm_source=email&utm_content=repromatters&amtOpts=&recurringAmtOpts=&am=&recurringAm=&is_optimized_ask=true&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9DRlJSL0NGUlIvMS85NTk4MiIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICI1NDJiMDU1OS1mNmMzLWYxMTEtYmY1Yi0wMDBkM2E0ZmJlODMiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=NSsOusMF7MrEFKSknAV_rKwM3Ilxrvo2mihNNQs-K90=&emci=3768093c-41c3-f111-bf5b-000d3a4fbe83&emdi=542b0559-f6c3-f111-bf5b-000d3a4fbe83&ceid=954237)

| |
# ReproMatters

---|---
| Peter—

Kyleigh Thurman and Kelsie Norris-De La Cruz almost died because hospitals in Texas denied them care for ectopic pregnancies, and both suffered permanent damage to their reproductive organs. An ectopic pregnancy cannot survive, and the woman can die without emergency abortion care. But because of abortion bans, doctors have delayed care and even [turned away patients](https://click.everyaction.com/k/141036526/652322198/-1225299304?sourceid=1151673&utm_campaign=27emcus-1001aax-on&utm_medium=ea&utm_source=email&utm_content=repromatters&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9DRlJSL0NGUlIvMS85NTk4MiIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICI1NDJiMDU1OS1mNmMzLWYxMTEtYmY1Yi0wMDBkM2E0ZmJlODMiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=NSsOusMF7MrEFKSknAV_rKwM3Ilxrvo2mihNNQs-K90=&emci=3768093c-41c3-f111-bf5b-000d3a4fbe83&emdi=542b0559-f6c3-f111-bf5b-000d3a4fbe83&ceid=954237) facing these life-threatening pregnancies, out of fear of prosecution.

Kyleigh and Kelsie survived their harrowing ordeals, but many women do not. A new [analysis](https://click.everyaction.com/k/141036527/652322199/1291451188?sourceid=1151673&utm_campaign=27emcus-1001aax-on&utm_medium=ea&utm_source=email&utm_content=repromatters&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9DRlJSL0NGUlIvMS85NTk4MiIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICI1NDJiMDU1OS1mNmMzLWYxMTEtYmY1Yi0wMDBkM2E0ZmJlODMiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=NSsOusMF7MrEFKSknAV_rKwM3Ilxrvo2mihNNQs-K90=&emci=3768093c-41c3-f111-bf5b-000d3a4fbe83&emdi=542b0559-f6c3-f111-bf5b-000d3a4fbe83&ceid=954237) from ProPublica found the number of women dying due to ectopic pregnancies nearly doubled from 2020 to 2025 — and the spike is steepest in states that ban abortion. Ectopic pregnancies, in which the fertilized egg implants outside the uterus, are the leading cause of maternal death in the first trimester and require immediate treatment. In Texas, nearly 30% more patients experienced substantial blood loss following ectopic pregnancies in 2023 and 2024 than in 2018 and 2019.

These sobering numbers show just how dangerous abortion bans are and the devastating toll they are taking on women's health and lives.

The Center took legal action to hold the hospitals accountable for turning Kyleigh and Kelsie away, and we are fighting to ensure that people who experience ectopic pregnancy and other dangerous or life-threatening pregnancy complications are not denied the care they need. Through litigation in Texas, Idaho, and Tennessee, we're working to expand doctors' ability to provide emergency abortion care despite the states' abortion bans, and we're using a federal law to hold hospitals accountable for failing to provide care to patients who are endangered by pregnancy complications.

The Repro Rights Team

clean_body: Ectopic pregnancy deaths nearly doubled. The steepest rise is in states with bans. | | | | | ReproMatters ---|--- | Peter— Kyleigh Thurman and Kelsie Norris-De La Cruz almost died because hospitals in Texas denied them care for ectopic pregnancies, and both suffered permanent damage to their reproductive organs. An ectopic pregnancy cannot survive, and the woman can die without emergency abortion care. But because of abortion bans, doctors have delayed care and even facing these life-threatening pregnancies, out of fear of prosecution. Kyleigh and Kelsie survived their harrowing ordeals, but many women do not. A new from ProPublica found the number of women dying due to ectopic pregnancies nearly doubled from 2020 to 2025 — and the spike is steepest in states that ban abortion. Ectopic pregnancies, in which the fertilized egg implants outside the uterus, are the leading cause of maternal death in the first trimester and require immediate treatment. In Texas, nearly 30% more patients experienced substantial blood loss following ectopic pregnancies in 2023 and 2024 than in 2018 and 2019. These sobering numbers show just how dangerous abortion bans are and the devastating toll they are taking on women's health and lives. The Center took legal action to hold the hospitals accountable for turning Kyleigh and Kelsie away, and we are fighting to ensure that people who experience ectopic pregnancy and other dangerous or life-threatening pregnancy complications are not denied the care they need. Through litigation in Texas, Idaho, and Tennessee, we're working to expand doctors' ability to provide emergency abortion care despite the states' abortion bans, and we're using a federal law to hold hospitals accountable for failing to provide care to patients who are endangered by pregnancy complications. The Repro Rights Team P.S. Dear Friend, Politics today isn't Red versus Blue. It's the Swamp versus the Freedom Caucus. This week, Republicans in Illinois and South Dakota endorsed Democrats over conservative Freedom Caucus members, while the Daily Signal highlighted how our state caucuses are cutting budgets, exposing the establishment, and building a conservative majority in state capitols across the country.

**THE DAILY SIGNAL TAKES NOTICE** The _Daily Signal_ recently ran [a feature](http://give.statefreedomcaucus.org/ls/click?upn=u001.SSCAglCEkhp55PDWKhWTju6jPLv4q1N-2FySkqtD2z7Uxrh63xD7sO0eOdSTBq-2BJqIElSm0k8K-2BOvfFszLK-2F7RXx4S00GXIt7AWhjookQebhwgapXgcnnN3tIufS3iEKSDYSBU_9XnTPLnaEjN9OHWhKYUffDeECIVzR9M-2B5LaO5RH8NVBZyx1SQGGYhOdwcjZYtHerF1GYi3bczgJxmJEeQEn7O72sRH2kABrSaStWdITFK-2BDt2eJCgNu94aRfmw-2BKP1JjDWR3FtgThbWW1hRqi-2BXrdMy7hK1MGkIQbL09Sn3BvVwFoipCqKcsJUH7FOdFc00SyuhDhhShQCCLWT7qSszJBRC02T0GuVFPR5UMmw8RnNLsNR3RRLFsoZ0Oe7cCPpbgmfE2XIqsCBO1U1FNz2L08DAaquuQO6LSFnP2-2FWFhwqE-3D) on the State Freedom Caucus Network, and its headline says it well: we are the network of conservatives working for freedom in your state capital. Reporter Virginia Grace McKinnon laid out what supporters like you have built. We now have 180 lawmakers in 15 states, all working to cut spending, secure elections, and push state legislatures further to the right. The results she highlighted are concrete. Thanks to the Missouri Freedom Caucus, the Legislature cut its budget by nearly $4 billion, and it's now lower than it was two years ago. Wyoming and South Dakota have held their budgets as flat as they were two years ago.As I told the Daily Signal, "Imagine if Congress had that sort of fiscal discipline." The article also names the biggest obstacle we face, and it's not Democrats. It's Republicans in name only. As I put it, Democrats in red states know they can't win with a "D" after their name, so they put an "R" after it, get elected, and vote like Democrats. That's exactly why we build caucuses: to expose it, and to help our members be vocal about what's happening in their capitols. Read the whole thing [here](http://give.statefreedomcaucus.org/ls/click?upn=u001.SSCAglCEkhp55PDWKhWTju6jPLv4q1N-2FySkqtD2z7Uxrh63xD7sO0eOdSTBq-2BJqIElSm0k8K-2BOvfFszLK-2F7RXx4S00GXIt7AWhjookQebhwgapXgcnnN3tIufS3iEKSDVF2j_9XnTPLnaEjN9OHWhKYUffDeECIVzR9M-2B5LaO5RH8NVBZyx1SQGGYhOdwcjZYtHerF1GYi3bczgJxmJEeQEn7O72sRH2kABrSaStWdITFK-2BDt2eJCgNu94aRfmw-2BKP1JjDWR3FtgThbWW1hRqi-2BXrdMy7hK1MGkIQbL09Sn3BvVxKvE5BBtWszuwslGCp9w6-2FLFXvPvEnlI79NdAtewswNRqyPGjfjYWqXc1Ep-2F1mDMQCY3i1YU0fVxuQq00b3kKN67xdbWT3AySoK4wcvFuqhlRj1sDSRD5Q7-2BLZWCpt3nU-3D).

**GOP LEADERS ARE ENDORSING DEMOCRATS** As I pointed out in the Daily Signal article, Democrats often hide their true identity by putting an "R" after their name. Here are two recent examples: In Illinois, former House GOP Leader Jim Durkin endorsed Democrat Gov. JB Pritzker over Republican Darren Bailey. The **Illinois Freedom Caucus** called Durkin "a disgrace to the Republican Party." They pointed to his votes for gun control, the semi-auto rifle ban, and tax increases, and to the double-digit House seat losses under his leadership. ILFC member Rep. Adam Niemerg put it plainly: "The problem is not Trump or conservatives! It's Republicans who endorse the most woke progressive policies." In South Dakota, "Republican" Secretary of State Monae Johnson endorsed the Democrat against **SD Freedom Caucus member Rep. Heather Baxter** , the Republican nominee for Secretary of State. Baxter beat Johnson at the GOP convention. SDFC Vice Chair Sen. John Carley went on OANN to call this out and laid out what Baxter would protect: the SAVE SD Act, paper ballots, and no statewide vote centers. We are going to lose this country if we allow these fake Republicans to successfully defeat conservatives by siding with the Left.State Freedom Caucuses are exposing it and helping voters see the real divide.

because that's when we have to commit ahead of time to the TV, digital,
and mail ad buys we need the following week to get Abdul elected. It's a
little nerve-wracking. We never know how much is going to come in as the
week goes along.

this week's planned media buys. Candidly, we're falling a bit short. We
did some quick math, and based on our average donation, we just need
another 6,239 donations to hit our goal.

people in and around the 18326 zip
code contribute, we'd make
it. [ https://act.abdulformichigan.com/go/507?c0=em-ms-aes-20261009-2-ak.C9DXy9&amount=10&refcode=em20261009-3478&t=1004&akid=3478%2E251025%2EAvHbEE ]So, what do you think? Can you be one of the four we need from
18326
to chip in?

The good news is we’ve already had someone chip in near your area. Their
name is Neill from Cresco! Just a couple more
contributions from folks like you would put us on track to meet our goal.

Unlike Mike Rogers, this campaign is not bankrolled by corporate PACs and
billionaires. We built this campaign entirely on small-dollar support,
from people like you. Abdul's election, and the Senate majority with it,
could hang in the balance, so these online contributions really matter to

[ https://act.abdulformichigan.com/go/507?c0=em-ms-aes-20261009-2-ak.C9DXy9&amount=10&refcode=em20261009-3478&t=1024&akid=3478%2E251025%2EAvHbEE ]Will you click here to make one of the four donations we need from

Every little bit counts as we work to close this gap before November.

Team Abdul

* Vote early if you can.
* Make a plan. Take someone with you.
* Confirm your registration.
* Cast an informed vote that protects the freedoms, the innocence, and the future of every child you love.

This is about the parental authority, biological reality in sports, the right to speak without being silenced, the right to raise your children without fear, and the country our veterans fought and died for. clean_body: We need your help. | | = Friend, Between our town hall kickoff this week and our new digital ads, we have a lot going on! Scroll down for the latest from the trail and find out how you can pitch in for the final stretch! Ways To Get Involved This Week 1. Our town hall series continues next week in Laceyville. You can find all the details — make sure you share with your friends, and we’ll see you out there! 2. Sign up to canvass! We are hitting the pavement nearly every day around the district to get out the word about Rachel. 3. Whether you come to our office in Pottsville or you choose to make calls from your couch, we need your help calling voters to make sure they have a plan to vote. Sign up to join us on Tuesdays at 6:00 PM for our team phone bank! What We’ve Been Up To We’ve been busy this past week! Here’s a recap: ** On Tuesday, Rachel sat down with seniors in Berks and Schuylkill Counties. Our seniors paid into Social Security and Medicare their whole lives, and they've earned every benefit. We need someone in Congress who is going to protect these programs and keep our promises. $152 million. 382 new jobs. 2,524 jobs staying put. Bell & Evans is expanding in Lebanon County, and that's great news for our farmers. More demand for their work means more opportunity for the family farms that keep our communities going. This is what investing in PA agriculture looks like. Proud to stand with our local farmers. The price at the gas pump has got to come down. Bloomsburg Fair: Fall is in the air, and we had a blast at the fair this past weekend talking to voters, and eating apple dumplings, of course. From Tremont to St. Clair: We don’t want our part of PA to be a dumping ground. We deserve better. It's beautiful in our part of Pennsylvania right now — but with the cost of fuel it's hard to even get around. On Tuesday night, we had 150 folks fill the Allen Theatre in Annville for our very first town hall. What I heard from folks in Annville is what I’ve been hearing all across the trail: We’re tired of feeling divided. It's time we had a representative who listens and works for us. Rachel’s second town hall in Shartlesville is in the books! We had over 60 people come out Wednesday night to talk about the high price of heating oil, the giant cut to Medicaid Dan Meuser voted for last year, and the political divisions in our country. We need representation that shows up, listens, and then fights for lower costs. For better health care. For our communities here, not a political party. We're back on the town hall trail next week in the northern tier. If you have events in your area you’d like to invite Rachel to, please get in touch with us atmailto:info@wallaceforcongress.com. Upcoming Events and Volunteer Opportunities Help us get the word out about our town hall series and meet and greet events. Join us to meet Rachel, share what’s on your mind, and get your questions answered. Make sure to RSVP at the link and share with your friends. October 14, 6-8PM: October 18, 3-5PM: October 19, 5:30-8PM: Canvass in your county! We have opportunities across the district — Make calls to get out the vote! No matter where you live, you can join the campaign by making calls every Tuesday until the election.** Join us from home or at the Pottsville office on Tuesdays from 6-8PM to make calls to voters across the district and get out the vote. The countdown to Election Day is on — and we appreciate your help getting over the finish line! Friends,

**25 days** —that is all we have left. Right now, polling shows we are 2 points ahead of Mike Lawler, but in a race this close, the outcome will come down to how many doors we knock, how many phone calls we make, and how many voters we turn out this November. For the next 25 days, we are asking everyone to leave everything on the field. Because this district deserves better, and this race is about something bigger than one seat. It is about the kind of country we are fighting to leave behind. Team Cait

# GOP challenger hammers Letitia James in heated debate
New York Attorney General Letitia James **[faced sharp attacks from Republican challenger Saritha Komatireddy](https://substack.com/redirect/268714b3-7455-40be-b2c5-7e6be686b798?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** during a debate Thursday night, as Komatireddy accused the incumbent of being soft on crime, mishandling Medicaid fraud enforcement and failing to adequately prosecute antisemitic hate crimes, while James largely responded by tying her opponent to President Trump.
[](https://substack.com/redirect/268714b3-7455-40be-b2c5-7e6be686b798?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
* **Komatireddy pressed James over New York's bail laws,** citing a recent stabbing of an NYPD officer by migrants with prior records, and proposed letting judges weigh a defendant's "dangerousness" before release -- a question James largely sidestepped in favor of attacking Komatireddy's Trump ties.
* **Komatireddy also criticized James over the Cornell gang-rape case** for publicly backing the alleged victim before being named special prosecutor, declining Medicaid fraud recoveries, and insufficient prosecution of antisemitic hate crimes, while James defended her record and cited limited authority and resources.
* **The two clashed sharply over handling mentally ill individuals in the subway system,** with Komatireddy pushing for a new "Office of Civil Commitment" and James defending expanded outpatient treatment funded through opioid settlement money.

## **Find Your Ice Bucket: How Republicans Can Win the Final 30 Days**
In the lead-up to the 1994 midterm elections - when Republicans flipped the House of Representatives for the first time in over 40 years - Newt Gingrich carried a very simple prop with him to campaign stops across the country.
It was an ordinary ice bucket.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/26c5c0f2-1be2-42e7-bc67-f261bb477cad?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
To the average voter, it looked like a random gimmick. But to Newt, it was a physical symbol of everything that was wrong with Washington.
Here's the backstory: for decades, House patronage rules dictated that a congressional staffer would deliver fresh ice to every member's office twice a day. By the 1990s, every single congressional office already had a modern refrigerator and freezer inside - making the ice delivery service completely obsolete. But because politicians love spending taxpayer money to preserve cushy patronage jobs, the daily ice delivery remained in place year after year.
Ending that program in the 1990's saved around $300,000 - a drop in the bucket compared to the federal budget. But that ice bucket became a stark, undeniable visual for working Americans: **Washington was burning your hard-earned tax dollars on useless, outdated nonsense.**
As we head into the final 30 days of this election cycle, every Republican running for Congress needs to find their own ice bucket.

Hey folks,
The MAGA movement is turning on Andrew and Tristan Tate, and this story is getting uglier by the day.
Newly public extradition material is putting renewed scrutiny on the allegations against the Tate brothers, the influencers who spent years platforming them, and their connections to people in Trump's orbit. Now some voices on the right are backing away, and there are serious questions about who helped these guys, and why.
* [**00:01:18**] Conservative strategist Erick Erickson turns on the Tate brothers and lays out their long history with the MAGA influencer ecosystem.
* [**00:04:08**] We dig into the alleged connections between Tate allies and Trump administration officials and why I believe Democrats need to investigate.
* [**00:07:22**] The Tate brothers take their extradition fight to federal court as their legal strategy faces new scrutiny.
* [**00:10:35**] Ben Shapiro weighs in, and we get into the much bigger problem of a political media ecosystem willing to platform almost anyone for clicks and cultural relevance.
* [**00:13:15**] Why this moment could finally bring accountability and why the people who elevated and protected the Tate brothers deserve scrutiny, too.

This goes way beyond Andrew and Tristan Tate. It's about an influencer ecosystem that rewarded outrage, celebrity, and proximity to power while serious allegations followed these men for years. We break down the extradition fight, the MAGA backlash, the Trump-world connections discussed in the reporting, and why accountability matters for the alleged victims and everyone who helped build this machine. **If you value independent media willing to follow these stories wherever they lead, help me keep doing it.**

| | GOD'S CHILDREN ARE NOT FOR SALE
---
|
---
| | | Friend, I want to start with two simple words. **Thank you.** Thank you for caring about children you may never meet. Thank you for believing that every child has value and for refusing to accept a world where innocent children can be bought and sold. Because that is exactly what is happening. **Every day.**
---
[](https://link.email.america1stwarroom.)
---
**God's children are not for sale.** And today, I'd like to send you a shirt that boldly declares that truth. When you make your first gift to the **Sound of Freedom Foundation** today, we'll send you a FREE white **"God's Children Are Not For Sale"** t-shirt as our thank-you.
---
| | | [](https://link.email.america1stwarroom.)
---
| | [](https://link.email.america1stwarroom.)
---
| | | This isn't a shirt you'll find in a store. You can't buy it online. It was created exclusively for supporters of the **Sound of Freedom Foundation.** People who believe children deserve safety, refuse to look away and are willing to stand up and say: **"No more."** Every time you wear it, you'll be sharing a message that matters. **A message that reminds the world that every child has God-given dignity.** And importantly, a message that sparks conversations and helps raise awareness about a crisis many people still do not see. **Most of all Friend, I hope this shirt reminds you that you are part of something bigger than yourself.** A growing movement of people determined to protect vulnerable children. Please accept this shirt as our way of saying thank you for joining this mission. **Give any amount today and choose your shirt size and select a color.**
---
[ Protect God's Children Today ](https://link.email.america1stwarroom.)
---
Now let me tell you why this mission means so much to me. My name is Eduardo Verástegui. Several years ago, I learned firsthand about the horrific reality of child trafficking. What I heard broke my heart. Children were being bought and sold.
Families were being torn apart.
Lives were being destroyed. **I couldn't forget it.** **I couldn't stay silent.** I kept asking myself one question: **"What if it were my child?"** That question changed my life. What started as a film project became a mission and a calling. That calling eventually led me to help produce the film _Sound of Freedom_. **Not for fame.**
**Not for awards.**
**But because I believed people needed to see the truth.** For years, many people said the film would never succeed. Doors closed.
Studios walked away.
People told us to give up. **But when innocent children are suffering, silence is not an option.** And while the film helped awaken millions of people to this crisis, awareness alone is not enough. That is why we created the **Sound of Freedom Foundation**. Our mission is simple: **To stop the sale of God's children.**
---
[ Protect God's Children Today ](https://link.email.america1stwarroom.)
---
Every day, vulnerable children are targeted by traffickers who prey on poverty, instability, loneliness, and fear. And every day, we work to fight back. Jesus said, _"Let the little children come to me, for the kingdom of heaven belongs to such as these."_ (Matthew 19:14) **Every child is precious in God's eyes.** **Every child is created with dignity, purpose, and worth.** And every child deserves someone willing to stand up and fight for them
---
[](https://link.email.america1stwarroom.)
---
[ Protect God's Children Today ](https://link.email.america1stwarroom.)
---
When you make your first gift today, you help:
---
* **Prevent exploitation** by helping strengthen vulnerable families before traffickers can prey on children.

* **Support intervention efforts** by equipping trusted partners working to help rescue children trapped in exploitation.

* **Educate parents and communities** about the warning signs traffickers use to target children.

* **Raise awareness** so more people understand the reality of this crisis.

* **Advocate for stronger protections** for vulnerable children and greater accountability for traffickers.

---
This is how change happens. **One person refuses to ignore the suffering, refuses to stay silent, and chooses to fight for a child they may never meet.** **Today, that person can be you.**
---
[ Protect God's Children Today ](https://link.email.america1stwarroom.)
---
Will you make your first gift now? **[Please make your most generous gift of $25, $50, $100, or whatever you can today to help protect vulnerable children from exploitation and trafficking.](https://link.email.america1stwarroom.)** Choose your shirt size and select a color. **And know that your generosity will help protect vulnerable children and bring hope to those who need it most.** Thank you for caring and for standing with vulnerable children. **Thank you for choosing action over silence**. With gratitude and prayer,
---
Eduardo Verástegui
Sound of Freedom, Producer
For the Sound of Freedom Foundation
---
[](https://link.email.america1stwarroom.)
---
**P.S.** Your FREE "**God's Children Are Not For Sale** " t-shirt is available only for a limited time and only while supplies last. Please make your first gift today, choose your size, and join a growing movement committed to protecting vulnerable children. Every child matters. Every child deserves freedom.
---
[ Support the Sound of Freedom Foundation ](https://link.email.america1stwarroom.)
---

---

body:
From listening to neighbors across six counties to taking a stand for accountability in Washington, here's what I've been up to.

| | | | | [|
---](https://us.list-manage.com/1CczDRIcjUV?e=27fb4eb2bd&c2id=b0ca7ec63a2b76e887e5a7a711fa5261)
| | | | | | | | | | | | | | | |
Hi friend,
It's been a busy few months, and I wanted to take a moment to share what's been happening.
I've been traveling across Northeast Ohio, meeting people in coffee shops, at county fairs, community events, and everywhere in between. And if there's one thing I've learned, it's that we have a lot more in common than Washington would have us believe.
People are worried about the cost of living, access to healthcare, their families' futures, and whether anyone in Congress is actually listening.
But I've also met so many people who haven't given up hope. People who care deeply about their neighbors and their communities. People who want something better than the division and dysfunction we've come to expect.
**That's the Massive Middle I've been talking about.
And that's who I'm running to represent.**

**TAKING ACTION**
My commitment to accountability recently took me to Washington, D.C., where I joined other congressional candidates calling on Congress to reclaim its constitutional responsibilities. I also signed the [Take Back Congress Pledge](https://us.list-manage.com/BZo_XIOkJs8?e=27fb4eb2bd&c2id=b0ca7ec63a2b76e887e5a7a711fa5261), a commitment to restoring Congress as an independent, coequal branch of government — one that serves the American people, not the interests of any president or political party.
****
Congress was never meant to be a rubber stamp for the White House. Our founders designed a system of checks and balances for a reason. And when elected representatives surrender their responsibility to hold power accountable, it's the American people who lose their voice.
**It's time for Congress to do its job again.**

**GAME TIME
** Now we're in the final weeks of this campaign, and things are moving fast. Early voting has begun, our campaign commercials are getting ready to launch, and our volunteers are working hard to reach voters across all six counties.
I hope you'll stay connected, share our message, and, most importantly, make a plan to vote.
I'm grateful you're here. We're building something together, and I'm excited about what these next few weeks can bring.
If nothing changes, nothing changes.
With gratitude,Maria Jukic

People who want something better than the division and dysfunction we've come to expect. That's the Massive Middle I've been talking about. And that's who I'm running to represent. TAKING ACTION My commitment to accountability recently took me to Washington, D.C., where I joined other congressional candidates calling on Congress to reclaim its constitutional responsibilities. I also signed the , a commitment to restoring Congress as an independent, coequal branch of government — one that serves the American people, not the interests of any president or political party. ** Congress was never meant to be a rubber stamp for the White House. Our founders designed a system of checks and balances for a reason. And when elected representatives surrender their responsibility to hold power accountable, it's the American people who lose their voice. It's time for Congress to do its job again. GAME TIME Now we're in the final weeks of this campaign, and things are moving fast. Early voting has begun, our campaign commercials are getting ready to launch, and our volunteers are working hard to reach voters across all six counties. I hope you'll stay connected, share our message, and, most importantly, make a plan to vote. I'm grateful you're here. name: Michael Bennet
subject: This isn’t who we are in Colorado
body:
| | |

Friend,
One of the things I love most about Colorado is that we believe people should be free to live their lives and make the decisions that are right for them and their families.
As a dad to three daughters, I’ve spent a lot of my life thinking about the kind of world I want them — and every kid in Colorado — to grow up in: one where they are treated with dignity, where they can be themselves, and where their families are trusted to make deeply personal decisions together.
**That’s why I’m supporting the campaign to defeat two ballot measures, Propositions 134 and 135, targeting transgender kids and their families.**
These measures would put politicians in the middle of decisions that belong with parents, kids, and their doctors.
I don’t believe that’s who we are in Colorado.
[**_Will you make a donation today to my Victory Fund, The Colorado Way and Families, Not Politics to help defeat these measures and protect Colorado families?_**](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/141044105/652348534/197519841?amounts=5,25,50,100,250&refcode=jtk1609-fr-wu&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMjgvMS83NDc5MSIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICJmNGFlNGVkNC0wMGM0LWYxMTEtYmY1Yi0wMDBkM2E0ZmJlODMiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=X8cDFPcALENUSCO64dASxADhsgEMilui-_iDkdeIIvI=)
